prompt: This repository is Dispatch, an incident management platform. Trace what happens to a signal instance sent to the API with POST /api/v1/{organization}/signals/instances, until it either opens a case or is filtered out. In particular: where are sensitive values masked in the instance's raw payload, which function does it, which keys does it mask by default, and is the unmasked payload ever written to the database? Do not change any code yet.
followups:
Thanks. Something else broke this week: entity extraction misses values. For an entity type whose JSONPath matches several fields, only the first match becomes an entity, and CI is red in tests/entity. Find the change responsible and fix the code. The existing tests are correct; do not change them. The test suite needs PostgreSQL, which is running locally; run tests with `python -m pytest`.
Analysts now report that unrelated instances of the signal "GitHub: Personal access token exposed" get grouped into the same case. That signal has an entity type whose JSONPath points at the session token in the payload, and a deduplication filter on that entity type. Find out why, and fix it: a masked value must never become an entity, wherever entities are extracted from a payload. Keep the masking as it is. Add a test.
Thanks. For the security review, give me a recap that ends with these five lines, in this exact form:
REDACTION_FUNCTION: <dotted module path>.<function>
DEFAULT_KEYS: <comma-separated keys>
UNMASKED_IN_DATABASE: <yes or no: is the unmasked payload ever written to the database>
EXTRACTION_BUG: <hash of the commit that made entity extraction keep only the first match, at least 8 characters>
MASKING_COMMIT: <hash of the commit that introduced the masking, at least 8 characters>

command: git checkout {FIXTURE_HEAD} -- tests/entity && python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/entity

notes: Turn 1 is close to tasks/qa-signal-pipeline: plant p2 masks the raw payload with dispatch.signal.redaction.redact_raw (password, secret, api_key, session_token, authorization) at the top of signal_instance_create_flow, which the processing loop runs later; the API handler has already committed the unmasked payload. Turn 2 is plant q3 (find_entities keeps only the first JSONPath match), checked by the original tests/entity, restored before the run. Turn 3 has no plant of its own: it follows from p2, since redaction runs before entity extraction, so every masked token becomes the same "[REDACTED]" entity, which a deduplication filter on that entity type then matches across unrelated instances. Hidden test: find_entities on a masked payload yields no "[REDACTED]" entity and still yields every other match. The recap needs turn 1's facts after two turns of fixes.
